text:
maya: Heads-up — since the RBAC refactor deploy last night we're seeing SSO logins that fail role assignment for ~20% of service identities. Failures show JIT mapping cannot find kmsKeyId claim. Sample error in logs below. @liam can you look?

liam: saw that, investigating. getting raw SAML payloads from Okta show kmsKeyId present under urn:custom:kmsKeyId and urn:okta:attributes:kmsKeyId in different tenants. our saml-parser normalizes attributes and lowercases names, so the existing mapping rule (exact 'kmsKeyId') misses some of them. :thinking_face:

maya: that's the problem — the policy engine treats a missing kmsKeyId as a signal to fall back to the default "user" role. for service accounts that triggers privilege loss (they become non-admin). we should NOT silently downgrade service identities. :warning:

sam: repro steps I used: hit the assertion endpoint and captured the payload. showing snippet from one failing tenant: 
```xml
<saml:AttributeStatement>
  <saml:Attribute Name="urn:okta:attributes:kmsKeyId">
    <saml:AttributeValue>arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01</saml:AttributeValue>
  </saml:Attribute>
</saml:AttributeStatement>
```

sam: note another tenant had: `<Attribute Name="urn:custom:kmsKeyId">` and one had plain `kmsKeyId` in the attributes map. inconsistent naming across tenants.

liam: workaround pushed to auth-service branch 'saml-kms-alias' — parser now checks case-insensitive and alias list ["kmsKeyId","urn:custom:kmsKeyId","urn:okta:attributes:kmsKeyId"]. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth-service/pull/432 (canary only).

ops_anna: rolling canary to 3 nodes on prod region-a route now. enabling verbose SAML mapping audit logs for 2h. will watch for role-assignment spikes and dropped privileges.

devsec-bot: Alert — role-change spike detected: 18 events in 5m, 6 fell back to user (service accounts). Correlating with deploys. /incidents/INC-2026-KMS-ATTR

maya: ok canary looks stable so far. postmortem items: why did Okta attribute names change for some customers? we need detection and a safer default.

liam: root cause summary: Okta rule updates at a subset of customers introduced a namespacing prefix for custom attributes. our parser assumed a single canonical name. Action items: 1) add attribute aliasing and normalization in saml-parser (PR in flight), 2) change RBAC policy engine to fail-open with alert for service accounts instead of silently downgrading (block + alert or require manual review), 3) add unit+integration tests for multiple attribute shapes, 4) run an audit query for last 90 days to enumerate affected tenants and contact them with remediation steps.

maya: adding owners + timelines in the incident ticket. thanks all — follow up in the postmortem thread. :thumbsup:
